open_issues: The W05/W06/W07 lock-out remains a convenience limit, not a security control: the counter lives in keys/session.dat (machine-scope DPAPI) inside a folder the host grants BUILTIN\Users Modify on, so a local account can still delete it. Deleting it no longer buys back the shortest wait (a missing card on an activated machine now starts at the second lock round), but an attacker who deletes it between every round still caps the wait at that second level instead of letting it double indefinitely. The dominant threat is an offline attack on installation.key, which this does not affect. Making it tamper-proof needs a store outside the installation folder, which is a decision for the owner.

The WPF window-level drop of a .wakeel-setup file still cannot be exercised from the test suite or over CDP (the WebView swallows drops over the content area); it stays covered only at the unit level.

A genuinely full disk cannot be staged in the suite. The new rollback test stages the equivalent failure (the database cannot be created) and proves the same code path; DiskSpace.IsFull itself is covered by its own unit tests.

ARCHITECTURE.md §3's machine-scope DPAPI MachineWrap with constant entropy is implemented exactly as the document mandates; whether that is the right decision is a specification question for the owner, not a defect in this package.
notes:
WHAT CHANGED, FINDING BY FINDING.

MEDIUM 1 — ActivationService has no rollback (src/Wakeel.UI/Services/Account/ActivationService.cs). ActivateAsync is now all-or-nothing. A local `committed` flag is set only after _session.Adopt has taken the finished installation over; every failure path — the DiskFull result and the general rethrow, both of which now run a new catch — calls RollBack(committed) first. RollBack deletes keys/installation.key together with its .tmp and .bak siblings and data/wakeel.db together with -wal, -shm and -journal, each delete swallowing IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException so a stuck file cannot hide the failure that brought us there. AlreadyActivated (key file OR database) guaranteed neither existed on entry, so this restores the pre-activation machine byte for byte and the next attempt starts from clean ground; the AlreadyActivated-vs-IsActivated asymmetry the review flagged is therefore no longer reachable. New walkthrough fact `An_activation_that_cannot_finish_leaves_the_machine_as_it_found_it`: a directory is placed where the database file has to go, so the attempt fails after WriteKeyFile; it asserts the throw, then that installation.key (and .tmp/.bak) is gone, IsActivated and AlreadyActivated are false, and then that the same staged file, the same sheet and the same recovery code activate the machine on the second try and both the password and the code still work afterwards. I verified the test is not a tautology by inverting RollBack's guard and re-running it: it fails on exactly the "key file is gone" assertion.

MEDIUM 2 — RecoveryService persisted before proving the database opens (RecoveryService.cs). RecoverAsync now opens DbSession with the recovered dbKey FIRST and only then derives the new password wrap, the new machine wrap and (when asked for) the replacement recovery wrap and calls keyFile.Save; the connection is disposed on any failure inside. A `saved` flag splits the two failure paths: before the save, the outcome is still DatabaseUnreadable and the key file is untouched, so the forgotten password and the old sheet are both still in force; after the save, the new outcome RecoveryOutcome.RecoveredNotSignedIn returns the new sheet plus one Arabic sentence (Ar.FirstRun.Recovery.SucceededNotSignedIn: the password has been set, save the new sheet, close الوكيل and open it again to sign in) — a recovery that happened is never reported as a failure, and a replacement code is never written and then discarded unseen. W07 handles that outcome: it clears the typed secrets, shows the new sheet for printing, keeps the sentence on screen, and does NOT raise OnRecovered, so nothing navigates into a workspace that is not open (a new _recoveredWithoutSession flag also gates CloseAsync). New walkthrough fact `A_recovery_that_cannot_open_the_installation_changes_no_secret` makes the database unopenable at exactly that moment and asserts either an untouched, byte-identical key file with the old password and old code still working, or — if anything did reach the disk — that the new sheet came back with the result. I confirmed the test takes the DatabaseUnreadable branch (temporarily failing the other branch and re-running it alone).

LOW 3 — W05 cached the lock-out (W05Login.razor). The standing lock is re-evaluated instead of cached: OnPasswordChanged and the top of SignInAsync clear _result when Login.LockedUntil() is null, so «دخول» re-enables the moment the announced wait is over. bUnit fact `The_sign_in_button_comes_back_by_itself_once_the_wait_is_over` renders the screen locked, checks the button is disabled and the sentence is shown, lets the wait expire, types, and asserts the button is enabled and the sentence gone.

LOW 4 — LockService key leak (LockService.cs). The catch around _session.Unlock now zeroes machineDbKey and machineVaultKey before returning DatabaseUnreadable; the finally still leaves the machine vault key alone on the success path, where the session owns it.

LOW 5 — W07 dropped keystrokes during verification (W07RecoveryDialog.razor). VerifyAsync keeps a pending-text field: text arriving while a check is in flight is remembered, and the running check loops and re-runs for it, so the last text typed is always the one that gets a verdict and a complete, correct code can no longer be left un-green. Short text now yields a null outcome (no error shown) rather than an early return. bUnit fact `A_code_finished_while_the_previous_one_was_being_checked_still_turns_green` fires two texts without waiting and waits for «تحقّق من الرمز» to appear.

LOW 6 — the counter can be deleted (SignInProfile.cs, LoginService.cs). SignInProfile gained a non-serialised Missing flag, set whenever Load falls back to a blank card (absent, unreadable, wrong version). RecordFailure raises LockRounds to at least 1 when the card is missing on a machine that is already activated, so throwing the card away no longer returns the wait to the shortest one; an honest person whose card cannot be opened pays nothing on a correct first attempt, and a successful sign-in resets everything as before. The residual limitation is recorded in open_issues.

LOW 7 — recovery codes were unlimited (RecoveryService.cs). Verify and RecoverAsync both refuse while a lock-out stands (new outcome LockedOut) and a wrong-but-well-formed code is counted through LoginService.RecordWrongPassword, de-duplicated against the last counted text so the per-keystroke checks and the new pending re-run never spend more than one attempt on the same code. A new instance method Explain() gives the same wait sentence the sign-in screen shows, with the minutes left; W07 uses it instead of the static Describe. New walkthrough fact `Wrong_recovery_codes_count_towards_the_same_wait_as_wrong_passwords` drives five wrong codes, asserts the wait now stands for the right code and for RecoverAsync, asserts that re-checking identical text costs no attempt, and then that once the wait is over the sheet recovers the account as it always did.

VERIFICATION. Exactly the prescribed command: dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop — 0 warnings, 0 errors; dotnet build tests/Wakeel.Walkthrough.Tests — 0/0; Walkthrough 18/18 (3 new); Core.Tests 175/175; UI.Tests 211/211 (2 new) — 404 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, warnings-as-errors clean. No NuGet package was added; nothing outside the allowed paths was touched (Ar.FirstRun.cs gained one constant; docs only the progress file).
